mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return discount, as investors anticipate rate hikes to curb future inflation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over the next 20 days, SPX 20d forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) despite inflation above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 monthly increases, signaling labor market strength that supports equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS > 200,000, 20d forward returns are not positive (p-value > 0.05) or the effect is smaller than the median positive effect across all labor strength regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 100) indicates weakening demand or supply-side headwinds, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 20d forward returns remain positive or the IC is not significantly below 0 (p > 0.05) when INDPRO is in contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500K for two consecutive months signals renewed demand for equities as confidence in the housing market recovers.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20d forward returns when HOUST remains above 1500 without a preceding two-month rise.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 60-day forward returns as lower rates encourage equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 20d forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of the low-rate regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) accompanied by a rise in monthly pay growth (implied by PAYEMS) creates a dual labor strength signal that drives positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC > 0.05) or 20d returns are not positive when both conditions hold.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in the catalog, so this sketch is omitted and replaced below with a regime-conditional supply effect). Instead: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 for four months indicates persistent supply constraints, predicting negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 20 days, SPX 20d returns are positive or the IC is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the four-month INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (money supply growth) accelerates above 10% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary accommodation that is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward returns when RSAFS > 10% for two months and other macro conditions are neutral.
